note: Atlas's machine interface. Every figure carries its signature — unit, basis, window, scope, counting — its as-of and the state the render gate assigned it. A `scenario` figure is authored: real, useful, and never admissible to a measurement aggregate. A `gap` is null WITH A REASON and is never a zero. A null signature component is the same thing one level down: its reason is on the referenced entry in `signatures`.
as_of_basis: oldest of 7 declared inputs (2026-07-28 to 2026-10-03); 2 inputs declare no as-of and are NOT covered by this date: form_map, pm_history/events.by-month-subject-cadence

writers.statement: The code that wrote the boards these figures were read from, by content digest. `inputs` pins the documents this export read; `writers` pins the code that wrote them, so a consumer holding two exports can tell a figure that moved with its writer edited from one that moved with its writer untouched. `attribution.rules` say which file writes which figure: rules are applied in order and the LAST MATCH WINS, because the boards are written in layers and the run order in scripts/rebuild-boards.sh decides the last writer. Every base rule is checked against design/data/atlas.json:continents.<name>.source where that declaration is a path; a prose declaration is reported in `undigested` WITH A REASON and never omitted. WHAT A DIGEST CANNOT SEE: an edit made and reverted between two exports, or a change in a module the generator imports, leaves the digest identical, so a movement it caused reads as unexplained. That errs towards reporting, which is the direction to err in.

attribution.statement: A figure's writer is the `path` of the LAST rule whose `continents` (null = any) contains the figure's continent and whose `fields` (exact names; null = any) or `field_prefixes` (null = any) admit the figure's field. A figure matching no rule stops the build that writes this document: a figure with no declared writer cannot be told from one whose writer was edited.

rule.statement: The published set is DERIVED, not chosen. (1) MEMBERS: a figure is a member of an aggregate iff its field is exactly `sub.usd` or begins with `cap.` — the board value of a cell, incumbent-held plus captured (gate/board.py:VALUE_FIELDS). `capFee`, `capSpr` and `capNtl` are other bases on the same money and are never members; `lat` is not board value; shares are not money. (2) BOARD HEADLINES: one `board:<continent>` for EVERY continent in atlas.json. No exclusions — a set with an exclusion is a set that was chosen. (3) POOL TOTALS: one `pool:<family>` for every family that has at least one continent whose role is `pool`; its members are drawn from the pool continents of that family only. A recut never enters a pool total, because its money is already counted in its source. (4) GATE STATE, in this order: an aggregate whose family is not summable across its own rows publishes null with the family's reason; otherwise, if its members' SIGNATURES differ the total is a gap whose reason names every component that differed and every value it took — the five components `parameters.signature` names, read off each member as published, except those the aggregate's kind ranges over (`parameters.signature.over`), which must be declared instead; an undeclared value is unknown and never a match; nothing licenses a difference but a conversion declared in conversions/registry.json (gate/algebra.py; NOT-250, operator decision D6); otherwise, if any member is a `gap` the total is a gap, because a sum that silently omits a withheld figure is not a total; otherwise, if every member is a `measurement` the total is a measurement; otherwise it is a `scenario` — an authored member makes the total authored, which is MS-30a transitivity. (5) VALUE: the rounded sum of the members' values, or null when the state is a gap.

cash_traded.monthly.not_summable_reason: twelve monthly figures; a continent-level total would carry a per-month unit on an annual quantity (quantity-algebra.md §2.7, §5)

signature.absence: a component part null on EVERY member is published under `undeclared` and does not refuse; null on some members and declared on others is a difference and refuses — an undeclared value is unknown, never a match

rule.statement: The coverage denominator is DERIVED, not chosen. (1) TEST: a leaf is `measurable` iff some observation of the world could settle its value — a party to the trade (a venue, an issuer, a filing, a regulator) could in principle report the quantity, whether or not anyone has. It is `judgment` iff no observation could, because the quantity is a reading imposed on the market, a counterfactual, or a decision Atlas took. (2) GRAIN: the test is applied at the FIELD FAMILY — the first dotted component of the leaf's field path — because that is the grain at which a quantity is declared. There are no per-leaf exceptions: every leaf of a family carries its family's class. (3) TOTALITY: a family absent from the table is a hard exit, never a default. A figure whose measurability nobody has stated stops the build. (4) NOT MEASURED IS NOT UNMEASURABLE: a family is `judgment` only for a reason about the world. That nobody has sourced it yet is a reason about Atlas's progress and makes it an unmeasured `measurable`, which is what the coverage figure is FOR. (5) REPORTING: coverage is published over both denominators — measurable and all — and the narrow one is never shown alone, because narrowing a denominator raises a percentage without measuring anything. (6) FALSIFIER: a `judgment` leaf that the render gate admits as a `measurement` refutes this classification and is reported, not absorbed.

addr.class_reason: 'addressable' is a decision about what Atlas would go after, not a property of the market; no observation can contradict it

addressable_row.class_reason: the addressable part of a row is the row's money times that decision, and a measurable quantity times a judgment is a judgment — the transitivity MS-30a applies to authorship, applied to measurability

cap.class_reason: what a named venue captured is that venue's own revenue; all 227 lineage records resolve to a venue-spend observation of exactly this quantity

capFee.class_reason: the fee half of capture is a published schedule times observed volume — the most directly reported quantity on the board

capNtl.class_reason: notional is the venue's own reported contract face. That two venues' notional may not be compared is a BASIS defect (atlas.json:notionalBasis), not a measurability one

capSpr.class_reason: the spread half of capture is observable from the book: quoted spread times volume, which is what the venue-spend producer already computes

eval.class_reason: terminal versus touch is a property of the contract's own terms, so the money under each is countable from the venue's published specifications

lat.class_reason: latent demand is money nobody spent — there is no observation of a trade that did not happen. The detector and falsifier beside it are what make it arguable, not measurable

motive.class_reason: no venue, counterparty or filing reports WHY a trade was placed; hedge/spec/gamble is a reading imposed on the flow, and two thirds of the cells are already a corner of the simplex rather than a proportion

oi.class_reason: open interest is the venue's own book — position notional outstanding, which Hyperliquid publishes per market. debt.statement: The dated debt register, by declared state, severity, blocker and review date, so the weekly digest can report debt BY STATE without a checkout. Each row counts the register's entries sharing all four. `state` and `severity` are the register's own declarations (spec/methodology/sourced-coverage.md); null where an entry declares none — counted and said, never defaulted. Whether a row is past its review date is the reader's question, against the reader's clock — this document knows no date (CLAUDE.md: nothing in the tree knows what time it is). Debt past its review date is REPORTED, never failed. A null review_date is a row with no clock on it, counted and said, never on time.

blockers.summary: The cell's world total is the sector's open interest in on-chain funding-rate futures, every venue that lists them. The one figure Atlas holds for the cell is Boros's own open-interest all-time high (~$250M, January 2026; atlas/cell_sources.py curated:boros-oi, from upstream/penetration/model.py:105): one venue's peak, on January's clock. It stood in world_total until 2026-10-02, under every later month. It is not the sector's world open interest on the overlay month's clock, so the world total is this gap and the reading is quoted as its reason.
blockers.unblocked_by: a source for the world open interest in funding-rate futures — every venue that lists them — stated for the overlay month; or Boros's own open interest sourced for the overlay month together with a sourced statement, for that month, that Boros is the whole market (the January peak satisfies neither)

blockers.summary: The cell's world VOLUME is sourced — BIS notional turnover, daily average over the month (NOT-190) — and its TradFi source, the CFTC COT legacy futures-only report, reports positions and open interest but no traded volume. So the TradFi capture on the volume metric is a gap: the exchange's own volume exists (CME daily bulletin) and is not wired, and it would need a declared comparison basis against BIS's daily-average notional before any share could be read.
blockers.unblocked_by: an exchange volume source for the COT-mapped contracts (CME daily bulletin or equivalent) on a stated basis, with the block's comparison_basis declared against the BIS figure

blockers.summary: The cell's TradFi capture is the CFTC COT legacy futures-only report's open interest on named CME contracts — one exchange's reading, attributed to the TradFi capture and not the sector's world figure. No free sector-level source exists for equity-index or commodity exchange-traded derivatives: the BIS statistics publish only foreign exchange and interest rate (NOT-190), and the FIA and WFE totals were investigated and rejected (NOT-167).
blockers.unblocked_by: a free, redistributable, machine-parseable world total for the sector's exchange-traded open interest, or a sourced statement that the COT-reported exchange is the whole market
